body:
Coordinator stopping rule (Termal::Fable2, 2026-11-24, from w-56f386fdd7d3 after 33 review rounds and 8 evaluations).

The launcher writes a run's request.json, results.json and other run files, and never rewrites them after its terminal write. A finding that needs those files REWRITTEN or REPLACED by something else after the terminal write is tampering. Under Greg's rule against hypothetical protections, it is not fixed in feature work: it is filed on w-3c1dd299f0f6 (run-file tampering), and the criterion states the premise explicitly, so evaluators judge against it rather than discovering it.

Still in scope and handled normally:
- removal of the run directory (cleanup, legitimate);
- files becoming unreadable (permissions, antivirus locks; environment);
- races between legitimate writers (the launcher, the host).

Why the rule exists: adversarial file-rewrite scenarios are unbounded. Without a stated premise, every review round can produce another Medium.
